units.text: Aspose.TeX FOSS for Python reads TeX input and converts it to output formats including .pdf, .dvi, and .svg. It writes .pdf and .dvi files directly to disk or returns their bytes in memory, and it writes .svg output to disk or returns the bytes of one or more SVG pages. The product provides a TeXJob class that executes TeX processing with configurable options and exposes messages for diagnostics.

It parses and interprets real TeX source through TeXJob, driving the tokenizer, macro expander, and mode-machine dispatch that process control sequences, groups, and paragraph text, then builds lines and pages from typeset boxes with a real line-breaking and page-building pipeline.

It produces output in PDF, DVI, and SVG formats by writing finished pages through PdfDevice, DviDevice, or SvgDevice, supporting file output via a Path or in-memory bytes when no destination is specified.

SvgDevice embeds glyph outlines straight from the bundled Computer Modern PFB fonts as path elements, so the rendered SVG needs no external fonts, and get_all_pages returns every page of a multi-page document as a list of byte strings.
It supports input from strings, files, and bytes via create_input_source.
It supports job diagnostics and logging by collecting run messages via TeXJob.messages and exposing a standard aspose_tex logger that can be configured with basicConfig and setLevel.
This example creates a PDF from a simple TeX string in memory and returns the PDF bytes in memory.
This example writes the PDF output directly to a file named hello.pdf on disk.
The following examples demonstrate converting TeX content to DVI, SVG, and PDF formats, as well as enabling logging for the aspose-tex-foss package.
Render TeX to DVI in memory.
Save DVI output to a file.
Render TeX to SVG in memory.
Save SVG output to a file.
Extract all pages as SVG bytes.
Render TeX to PDF with options.

The primary entry point is aspose_tex.TeXJob, which combines an input source, an output device (aspose_tex.PdfDevice, aspose_tex.DviDevice, or aspose_tex.SvgDevice), and aspose_tex.TeXOptions into one runnable job.
InputSource class serves as a base for input sources.
